title: Beatrix and the Cipher Revisited
premise: Mara Sandoval, an insurance investigator whose photographic memory has made him the quiet keeper of Hollow Creek's secrets, receives two letters from the same dead woman: one confessing to arson and fraud, the other promising a second confession if he can find her. Following a cipher hidden in the town's insurance ledgers, Mara discovers that Beatrix Vane faked her death three years ago—the same night his own files were quietly purged—and that the 'witness' everyone swears is dead is actually living among them under a new name. As Mara closes in, he must choose between exposing the conspiracy that includes the mentor who protected him, or burning the letters and keeping the town's fragile peace intact. In the end, Mara publishes only half the truth, finds Beatrix alive, and realizes belonging sometimes means carrying a secret rather than solving one.
about_author: Ada Amberdale is the pen name of a former claims adjuster who spent a decade reading other people's misfortunes in triplicate before turning to fiction. She writes mysteries from a converted fire station in the Pacific Northwest, where she keeps every rejection letter alphabetized.

chapters.title: Twin Envelopes
chapters.summary: POV: Mara. On the anniversary of Beatrix Vane's death, Mara receives two letters in her handwriting—one confessing to the mill fire, one promising 'the rest, if you can find me.' His photographic memory confirms both are authentic. Emotional beat: unease; the ordered world of his filing system cracks open with a single envelope.

chapters.title: The Alphabet of Ash
chapters.summary: POV: Mara. Reopening the cold Vane file, Mara notices anomalies only he could catch: ledger entries keyed to a cipher based on the Dewey decimal system she used as town librarian. The original claim was paid to a beneficiary who never existed. Emotional beat: obsession kindling; the investigator becomes the investigated mystery's servant.

chapters.title: Everyone Swears She's Dead
chapters.summary: POV: alternating Mara and Sheriff Dolan. Mara interviews townsfolk who recount Beatrix's funeral with suspiciously identical phrasing—rehearsed testimony. Dolan warns him off, gently at first. Emotional beat: creeping paranoia; grief in Hollow Creek feels manufactured, loyalty curdling into something enforced.

chapters.title: The Purged Drawer
chapters.summary: POV: Mara. Mara discovers his own archive was tampered with three years ago—pages removed the night of Beatrix's 'death'—and the signature on the disposal order belongs to his mentor, Edith Kroll. Emotional beat: betrayal; the man who kept others' secrets learns someone kept secrets from him.

chapters.title: What Edith Knows
chapters.summary: POV: Edith. Edith reflects on the night she destroyed the pages to protect Mara from what they implicated: the mill fire was arson committed by the town's founding families to collect on failing assets. Emotional beat: guilt and tenderness; protection revealed as complicity.

chapters.title: Cipher in the Stacks
chapters.summary: POV: Mara. Decoding the full cipher in the abandoned library, Mara maps a trail of payments and a name: 'R. Finch,' a witness who signed the original fire report then vanished. Cross-referencing, he realizes Finch never left town. Emotional beat: exhilaration shadowed by dread; each answer narrows the noose.

chapters.title: The Second Letter Arrives Early
chapters.summary: POV: Mara. Before Mara can act, the second letter appears on his desk—delivered by someone else. Someone knows he's decoding, and the promise inside turns to threat: stop, or become the next filed-away person. Emotional beat: fear; the hunter marked as prey.

chapters.title: R. Finch, Alive and Local
chapters.summary: POV: Mara. Mara identifies Finch as the unassuming hardware store owner who has sold him lightbulbs for years. Confronted, Finch admits witnessing the arson but insists Beatrix orchestrated her own disappearance to survive it. Emotional beat: vertigo; the town's kindness re-read as surveillance.

chapters.title: The Lighthouse Confession
chapters.summary: POV: Mara. Following the cipher's final coordinate, Mara meets Beatrix alive at the derelict lighthouse. She confesses everything—including that she sent the letters to force the truth out before the founding families finish burying it permanently, with Mara next. Dolan arrives armed behind them. Emotional beat: climax; truth and danger converge in salt wind and dark.

chapters.title: Half the Truth, Whole Heart
chapters.summary: POV: Mara. Mara outmaneuvers Dolan, exposes the arson and the founding families' fraud—but omits Beatrix's survival, letting the town believe its dead woman finally testified. He helps her vanish properly this time, on her terms. Emotional beat: bittersweet resolution; Mara learns that belonging isn't invisibility—it's choosing which truths to carry for the people you keep.
